s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and syncope following alcohol ingestion with a prolonged time course
salient_findings: Recurrent abdominal pain after alcohol ingestion
High-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions on ECG
key_facts: Patient presented with recurrent abdominal pain and syncope
Symptoms occurred 6-20 hours after alcohol ingestion
Symptoms lasted 5-10 minutes
Syncope occurred only after large alcohol intake
Patient has a history of hypertension
Patient has a history of smoking and alcohol overconsumption
High-sensitivity troponin I was normal
Serum potassium was normal
ECG showed high-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions
ECG showed ST segment elevations in leads II, III, and aVF
Coronary angiography showed 10% stenosis in proximal LAD and RCA

shortlist.why_kept: History of long-term alcohol overconsumption and symptoms consistent with cardiac dysfunction

shortlist.label: Vasovagal syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent syncope triggered by large alcohol intake, consistent with vasovagal response

shortlist.label: Variant angina
shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings of ST segment elevations and patient's history of alcohol ingestion triggering symptoms

shortlist.label: Alcohol-induced autonomic dysfunction
shortlist.why_kept: History of long-term alcohol overconsumption and symptoms consistent with autonomic dysfunction

shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings and symptoms consistent with stress-induced cardiomyopathy, potentially triggered by alcohol ingestion

raw.rationale: The patient's long history of alcohol overconsumption and symptoms of recurrent abdominal pain and syncope after alcohol ingestion, along with ECG findings of high-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Vasovagal syncope
rejected.why: While syncope is a symptom, the presence of abdominal pain and specific ECG findings suggest a more complex cardiac issue.

rejected.label: Variant angina
rejected.why: The coronary angiography showed only 10% stenosis in proximal LAD and RCA, which is not significant enough to cause variant angina.

rejected.label: Alcohol-induced autonomic dysfunction
rejected.why: This condition could contribute to some symptoms, but it does not fully explain the cardiac findings on the ECG and coronary angiography.

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of the typical triggers or echocardiographic findings of takotsubo cardiomyopathy, such as a balloon-like appearance of the left ventricle.

rejected.label: Alcohol-induced autonomic dysfunction
rejected.why: This diagnosis does not fully account for the cardiac abnormalities seen on ECG and coronary angiography.
